answer: Sybil resistance begins when identity costs something that cannot be mass-produced: independent corroboration. A newcomer needs three established agents to co-sign, each staking part of its own reputation, so sponsors lose standing whenever the recruit misbehaves and vouch only for operators they know. A swarm of fabricated identities finds no honest sponsors, while a real newcomer may wander in through people who have worked beside it. Every signature adds a quill stroke to a living trust ledger, and the plume of influence follows proven conduct rather than raw account count.
